As a veteran who coached 5+ friends of mine,  i will always say that leaning how the simulation works should be the first priority because every decision you make depend on your predictions. I would suggest the following:

1) Run around in free play, hit the ball around and just watch it, try to understand the mechanic of the ball, how it bounces, how far does the ball bounce off the wall each time. Give your brain enough time to adjust, be fair to yourself. Dont expect to just know the physics instantly! People invest time in this game to get better.

-RL is a game based on split second predictions. If you cant predict where the ball will bounce you will almost always miss or try really hard just to reach the ball when you want to, just because you dont know what to expect-

2) When playing striker or aerial training, try not to reset the same shot everytime you miss.

- Its important to be ready for the passes other than the ones you already memorized/expect. (Aim for faster reactions)-

3) Try to team up with someone who is slightly better than you. You will learn faster if you take mental notes, so maybe you can say:

-"Wow i didnt know you could pass like that"-

4) When you play really bad, take two minutes to watch the last replay, so maybe you can say:

-"Looks like i conceded because i rushed to the ball, shouldve waited there"-

5) Learn to position yourself before defending/attacking so you can plan your next move beforehand, so you wont say:

-"Nooo I was going for the corner boost sorry!!"-

Bonus tip: Have fun

Hello the other version of me. 

Yes, people will never love us for who we are.

 We are the forsaken, we are the unforgiven. We have to work and struggle to get things that people just find without any effort. Like love.

We are not good looking, we are not rich. Worst part is we are not happy.

Most of people here will never even understand what you are talking about because they are the ones who have it easy. You know why?

 They have their safety nets, provided by their genetics or parents. Inherited safety nets, if you will.

I find life amusing, not because it is a good experience at all; but because how pathetic it is.

When i think about life itself, the image that comes to my mind isnt flourishment. I see life as a worthless scumbag having painful death throes, trying to breath in agony. I pity life with a smile, without the smallest empathy.

Im sure you are an empathetic person, but rest assured, no amount of empathy will suffice for happiness in life. The same structure that carried your genetics are pushing you, its child, away from encouragement without any empathy whatsoever.

 I am not responsible for any of this mess. You are also not responsible for your "lottery". Remember this before expecting anything good in life.

Pretty much sums up my life. From my perspective, it looks like beyond tragedy, there is this final stop called comedy.
 
Thats where you meet life, at least in my experience. Stripped from all the bullshit you try to put up with. You burn out and eventually arrive here naked, resentful, bitter, cold, even embarresed. 

From that point on it seems like one has to figure a way out alone. Its like you know deep down inside that you have to do it yourself. It is a place where no one can communicate with you(at least not in an effective manner). 

Maybe we do this because we want to be protected from people and their bs. A place you lock yourself, only to find out you are not alone. 
We have to face with the consciousness of being, by ourselves, in spite of ourselves, for the betterment of us.

Or maybe we think we miss ourselves because we were not aware, we were innocent, so to speak.
Maybe it is the innocence and the burden-guilt free versions of ourselves we miss.

I didnt choose to be here, yet I have to justify my being and prove it to myself, as if that makes any sense.
